audio_script: A mass hangs from a spring. Release it from rest: why does it bounce, and why does the bounce fade? First isolate the mass. Gravity pulls down. The stretched spring pulls up, with a force proportional to how far it is stretched beyond its natural length. The solver adds these forces, divides by the mass, and uses Newton’s second law to update position and velocity with a fourth-order Runge-Kutta integrator. The zigzag spring follows the moving mass. Cyan shows velocity; green shows net acceleration, not another force. The arrows are schematic, while the readout gives model time, position, and speed. The drag term opposes motion, converting mechanical energy into thermal energy in the surroundings, so each swing is smaller. Remove drag and the ideal model keeps oscillating. Change the stiffness, mass, or damping in the CSV and the same simulation primitive draws a different experiment. This is a model: it assumes a massless spring and one-dimensional motion.
